s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic heel pain with limited response to treatment
salient_findings: Recurrent heel pain after surgical interventions
Tight gastrocnemius muscle with positive Silfverskiöld test
Pedunculated bony protrusion on the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus
key_facts: 41-year-old man with long-standing left plantar heel pain
Symptoms persisted for over two and a half years
Previous treatments included physiotherapy, anti-inflammatory and analgesic medications, and two surgical releases
Temporary relief from symptoms after treatments
Recurrent heel pain upon return to work
Antalgic gait observed on examination
Gastrocnemius muscle remained tight
Non-specific tenderness over the plantar aspect of the calcaneus
Normal bony relationships on weight-bearing radiographs
No fractures, lesions, or signs of arthritis on radiographs
MRI showed no thickening of the plantar fascia and no signal alteration in adjacent soft tissues or bone marrow
MRI revealed a pedunculated bony protrusion on the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus

shortlist.label: Haglund deformity
shortlist.why_kept: Pedunculated bony protrusion on the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus

shortlist.label: Calcaneal spur
shortlist.why_kept: Bony protrusion and chronic heel pain

shortlist.label: Intraosseous calcaneal lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bony protrusion and possible soft tissue involvement

shortlist.label: Calcaneal stress fracture
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic heel pain and bony abnormality

raw.rationale: The MRI revealed a pedunculated bony protrusion on the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus, which is consistent with a calcaneal spur, a bony growth that can cause heel pain.

rejected.label: Haglund deformity
rejected.why: Haglund deformity typically involves a bony prominence on the posterior aspect of the calcaneus, which does not match the location of the bony protrusion in the MRI findings.

rejected.label: Osteoid osteoma of the calcaneus
rejected.why: Osteoid osteoma typically presents with a characteristic nidus on imaging, which was not mentioned in the MRI findings.

rejected.label: Intraosseous calcaneal lipoma
rejected.why: Intraosseous lipoma would likely show signal alteration on MRI consistent with fatty tissue, which was not observed.

rejected.label: Calcaneal stress fracture
rejected.why: A stress fracture would likely show signs of fracture or bone marrow edema on the MRI, which was not present in the findings.
